name: Klaverjassen
description: Klaverjassen (also spelled Klaverjas) is one of the most popular card games in the Netherlands, traditionally played in cafes, social clubs, and at home. It is a trick-taking game for four players in partnerships, characterized by its unique trump ranking (where Jack and Nine are the highest cards) and the scoring of 'roem' (bonus points for card combinations). The game has several regional variants named after Dutch cities: Amsterdam, Rotterdam, and Utrecht.

content.text: Klaverjassen (also spelled Klaverjas) is one of the most popular card games in the Netherlands, traditionally played in cafes, social clubs, and at home. It is a trick-taking game for four players in partnerships, characterized by its unique trump ranking (where Jack and Nine are the highest cards) and the scoring of 'roem' (bonus points for card combinations). The game has several regional variants named after Dutch cities: Amsterdam, Rotterdam, and Utrecht.

Klaverjassen developed from the Jass family of games that originated in the Low Countries. The name comes from 'Klaverjas' (Jack of Clubs), reflecting the importance of the Jack in trump. The game became the dominant card game in the Netherlands during the 19th and 20th centuries.
4 players in partnerships, partners sitting opposite each other.
32-card Piquet deck: 7, 8, 9, 10, Jack, Queen, King, Ace in each suit. Dutch cards often use A (Aas), H (Heer), V (Vrouw), B (Boer) for indices.

Deal in three groups: first 3 cards each, then 2 cards each, then 3 cards each. Alternatively, deal in two groups of 4 cards each.

items.text: Amsterdam Rules: More flexible trump play; can throw off when partner is winning.
Rotterdam Rules: Must always play trump if cannot follow; must beat existing trumps.
